answer: Because the haven hash is checked against the gale checkpoint at intake, the anchor audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator forfeits authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 358 aliases cost 199 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
